findings.title: Denial cache is checked before the permission-allow cache, so a stale denial overrides a fresh allow
findings.body: In Check, the permDenialCache lookup (line 117) runs before consulting permCache via getCachedIdentityPermissions. A denial entry is written whenever a fresh DB lookup denies (line 154) and lives for shortCacheTTL (30s). If a user is denied, then granted permission, and the permission cache is subsequently refreshed with the new allowing permissions (e.g. by a concurrent Check for another resource of the same action that falls through to getUserPermissions and repopulates permCache), a later Check for the originally denied resource still hits the stale denial entry first and returns Allowed=false without ever looking at the now-correct permCache. Given the stated goal of this PR is to let creators access newly created resources quickly, the allow check should take precedence over the denial cache (or the denial entry should be invalidated when fresh permissions are stored), otherwise users can be denied for up to 30s despite correct permissions being cached.

findings.title: Test case 'should return error if store fails' never triggers a store error and asserts NoError
findings.body: In TestService_getUserPermissions, the case named 'should return error if store fails' sets permissions to nil but never sets err: true on the fakeStore, and the test body unconditionally calls require.NoError(t, err). The test therefore exercises a successful empty-permissions lookup, not a store failure, so the error path of getIdentityPermissions is untested and the test name is misleading.
